---
title: "Before the session"
---

Two things are needed before the session, and each ends in something that you can check: the case study read, and the browser lab opened once on the machine that you will bring. Together they take about an hour, and there is nothing to install and nothing to register for.

## 1. The case study

[Read the case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The case study presents the original study, with its questions, data and selections, then SCORE and the Multi100 project, the five reanalyses and how their results were put on one scale. The session works on this case throughout and can give it only a few slides, so read it before you come. The [exercise overview](../../cases/eu-frames/exercise.qmd) adds the table of what the five analysts found.

## 2. The browser lab

[Open the browser lab at Task 1](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-1-setup){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The browser lab is a page of this site on which R runs inside your browser, with the data already in place. Open it the evening before the session, on the machine and in the browser that you will bring, wait until the first cell shows a "Run Code" button, and run the three cells of Task 1. If the second reports 270 rows, 27 countries and 10 years, you are set, and your browser keeps the files that the lab downloaded, which matters where the Wi-Fi of a venue is slow. If the lab does not load, try another browser, and tell the facilitator before the session.

**By the start of the session** the browser lab loads on the machine that you will use, and you know what the claim is and how far apart the results of the five analysts are.
